about: Renders a form from a JSON Schema, or from fields written by hand, with the library's controls. The schema picks each field's control, the presentation lays the fields out, and every word comes from the catalogue under the form's identifier.

website.format: Enter a web address like https://example.com.

invoices.minLength: Enter the address invoices go to.

vat.pattern: Enter a VAT number like NL123456789B01.

elsewhere.label: Send invoices to another email address

vat.description: Two letters for the country, then the number.
vat.label: VAT number

note.description: Printed on a card in the box.
note.label: Gift note

conditional.about: Fields the schema declares under a condition, through `if` and `then` in `allOf`. The company and its VAT number appear for a business account, and the invoice address appears once the box is ticked.
conditional.title: Conditional fields

confirmation.about: A new password typed twice. The confirmation states `"x-matches": "password"`, a keyword the form's engine registers through `createEngine`, so the schema refuses a confirmation that differs, together with every other rule. The schema runs on submit and, after a refused submit, on every change, so the error goes as soon as the two match. Each box has a button that shows the password.
confirmation.title: Password confirmation

size.enum: Choose the size of your company.

controls.about: Each control a schema picks. A string renders a text box whose kind follows `format`, `format: "password"` a password box with a button that shows it, a number a number input, `format: "date"` a date input, an `enum` of up to five choices a radio group, up to ten a select and more a combobox, an array of choices a group of checkboxes, and a boolean a checkbox. The presentation names the textarea and the switch.
controls.title: Controls

floating.about: Labels that rest inside each empty text box and rise above it once the box takes focus or a value, through `orientation="floating"` on the form. The label keeps its row, so nothing under the field moves. The select keeps its label above it, because its trigger shows the choice or the placeholder.
floating.title: Floating labels

glyphs.about: The same form with lucide glyphs and with none. The form passes its glyphs to every field that renders a mark. Without them, a select has no chevron, a checked box shows its fill alone, a number input has no steppers, and a closed group has no chevron.
glyphs.title: Glyphs

customer.label: Customer
customer.missing: Enter who the invoice is for.

invoice.reminder: Remind the customer a week before the due date

layout.about: A fieldset per group, named by its legend and opened by a hairline, with twice the gap of the fields around it. The contact group lays its fields out in a row, the address group in two columns with the street across both, and the gift note starts closed. Two columns fold to one where the fields do not fit. Most fields are required, so the form marks the optional ones, and the postcode box is short.
layout.title: Groups and columns

size.enum: Choose the size of your team.

terms.label: I accept the terms of service

workspace.description: Everyone you invite sees this name.
workspace.label: Workspace name

iban.format: Check the IBAN: its check digits do not match.

digest.description: One email with everything from the day.
digest.label: Daily digest

hour.description: From 0 to 23, in your time zone.
hour.label: Digest hour

presented.about: Controls a presentation picks through `control`: cards with the words the catalogue gives under each choice, segments for a short choice, a slider for a bounded number, a date picker with a calendar, and checkbox cards for several choices.
presented.title: Controls a presentation picks

register.taken: An account with this email address exists. Sign in instead.

repeat.about: A group rendered once per item of an array, from the `minItems` to the `maxItems` the schema states. Each remove button is named by its item's number, and focus moves into an item after an add or a remove.
repeat.title: Repeat group

remember.label: Keep me signed in on this device

size.about: Every size. The size sets the gap between the fields, and every field of the form takes it.
size.title: Sizes

start.minLength: Choose the day the subscription starts.

descriptions.audit: Every change to the workspace, kept for a year.
descriptions.sso: Sign in through your identity provider.
descriptions.support: A reply within four working hours.

descriptions.business: Unlimited projects, with roles and single sign-on.
descriptions.starter: One project, for trying things out.

summary.about: A form validator refuses the whole value. The form's own error shows in the region above the fields, which takes focus, and a rule across two fields shows its error on the second. The address ada@example.com is taken.
summary.title: Form errors

tabs.about: The steps as tabs. A person moves between them in any order, focus remains on the tab, and the submit button follows the panels.
tabs.title: Tabs

title: Form

typed.about: Values a person types into a shape. More than ten countries render a combobox that narrows as a person types. The phone number takes the binding's `phone` format, and the form stores it in E.164. The postcode is masked as `9999 AA` through `control: "mask"`, and the skills are tags.
typed.title: Masks, phone numbers and tags

wizard.about: One step at a time. Next validates the step and moves focus to the next step's heading, Back validates nothing, and the last step shows the submit button.
wizard.title: Wizard

written.about: A form built from the library's own options, with each field written in `form.AppField` and its words passed as props. The customer's validator runs on blur and on submit.
written.title: Written by hand
